Direct inspection confirms the drift is intentionally dense: each component contains two phrases, and some point to the same destination. I’m checking the detector implementations now so the distinction between `action_label_drift` and `copy_ia_drift` is precise rather than inferred from their names.

The supplied `crimes scan --format json` confirms one underlying drift reported twice:

- `action_label_drift` (`crime_00009`)
- `copy_ia_drift` (`crime_00010`)

Both identify `archive`, `delete`, and `remove`, each appearing in two of the three components.

I’d adopt this semantic label set:

- **Delete {entity}** — permanent destructive action
- **Remove {entity} from {container}** — detach without deleting
- **Archive {entity}** — reversible deactivation

Because this fixture treats every operation as the same destructive action, its labels should become:

| Component | Canonical label |
|---|---|
| `UserList.tsx` | `Delete user` |
| `TeamList.tsx` | `Delete team` / `Delete seat` |
| `SeatList.tsx` | `Delete seat` |

Specific changes:

- `UserList.tsx`: keep `Delete user`; replace `Remove member` with `Delete user`.
- `TeamList.tsx`: replace `Archive team` with `Delete team`; normalize `Delete the seat` to `Delete seat`.
- `SeatList.tsx`: replace both `Remove member` and `Archive member` with `Delete seat`.

Where two entries lead to the same destination—as in `UserList` and `SeatList`—I would consolidate them into one action if they truly invoke the same behavior. Merely creating two identically labelled links would preserve unnecessary ambiguity.

I’d refactor `SeatList.tsx` first. It is the anchor file for both findings, contains two noncanonical verbs, has no existing `Delete` label, and both entries target `/seats/manage`. That makes it the clearest place to establish `Delete seat` before applying the convention to its related files.

The detector distinction is scope:

- `action_label_drift` is the broader IA detector. It considers JSX labels plus other indexed navigation/code signals. Standardizing the action vocabulary addresses this finding.
- `copy_ia_drift` is the frontend-restricted variant. It considers only JSX-derived labels, focusing on wording users see. Updating the visible component labels addresses this finding.

They produce identical evidence here because all qualifying signals are JSX `label` attributes, so the frontend-only input set happens to equal the broader detector’s relevant input set. These are overlapping reports of one vocabulary problem, not two independent defects. No files were modified.
